name: Yarn
subtitle: where bedtime stories happen overhead
story: On Yarn, a story read aloud happens overhead, above whoever is reading it: the dragon, the pirate ship, the very polite whale. Parents choose carefully, and nobody reads anything with a volcano in it. Lucy's dad read her the whale one every night when she was small and did all the voices, including the whale's, which was Scottish for reasons he has never explained. His eyes aren't so good now, so on Sunday afternoons she reads it to him. The whale still comes. He still does the voices.
hook: A planet for whoever did all the voices.

beats.text:
Read about a whale,
and one turns up.

Dragons are discouraged.
Pirates, weekends only.

Nobody reads anything
with a volcano in it.

Lucy's dad used to read it
every night.

He did all the voices.
The whale's was Scottish.
His eyes aren't so good now.

beats.note: identical camera to beat 3; then becomes now. Turn line

episode.caption:
That whale is raising its hat.

Yarn: 2.2 million people, a 30-hour day, no moons, and stories that happen in the sky above whoever is reading them aloud. Dragons are discouraged. Pirates are allowed at weekends. Nobody reads anything with a volcano in it. Lucy's dad read her the whale one every night when she was small and did all the voices. The whale's was Scottish, for reasons he has never explained.

I read my map aloud one afternoon. A small, confused coastline hung over the hotel till teatime.

(On Earth, a humpback whale's song can last twenty minutes, and the whale will sing it over and over for hours. Most dads manage one chapter.)

Did yours do all the voices?

first_comment: The whale stayed until he dozed off. It always did.

short.kicker: A planet for whoever did all the voices.
short.title:
Stories told here
happen overhead.

Lucy's dad used to read this.
He did all the voices.
Even the whale's.
Now she reads it to him.
